stem: For $\mathbf{a}=6\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b}=4\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}$, find the magnitude of $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$.
A particle moves at constant velocity from $2\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}\,\mathrm{m}$ to $9\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j}\,\mathrm{m}$ in $4\,\mathrm{s}$. Find the magnitude of its velocity.

A velocity changes at constant acceleration from $3\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ to $7\mathbf{i}+(-4)\mathbf{j}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in $4\,\mathrm{s}$. Find the magnitude of the acceleration.
Find the constant velocity when displacement changes from $2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}\,\mathrm{m}$ to $8\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j}\,\mathrm{m}$ in $3\,\mathrm{s}$.
A particle moves at constant velocity from $\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$ m to $13\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j}$ m in 4 s. Find its speed.
A particle moves from $2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ m to $8\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j}$ m in 3 s at constant velocity. Find its velocity.
